questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to argue a case you initially disagreed with. How did you approach it?

key_points: Understood client's position thoroughly despite disagreement
Maintained professional integrity while advocating zealously
Research-backed arguments even on unfavorable positions
Managed client expectations about likely outcomes
strong_answer_signals: Balances zealous advocacy with ethical obligations
avoid: Not fully committing to the client's position

questions.text: Describe a time you had to manage a heavy deadline while juggling multiple cases. How did you prioritize?

key_points: Assessed each matter by urgency and consequence (e.g., statute of limitations)
Delegated or restructured tasks where possible
Communicated delays or risks to clients and co-counsel
Delivered all critical work without compromising quality

questions.text: How would you handle discovering a factual error in a brief you already submitted to the court?

key_points: Assess whether error is material to the outcome
File a motion or errata notice immediately
Inform supervising attorney if applicable
Correct internally to prevent recurrence
avoid: Only fixing if caught by opposing counsel

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had an ethical dilemma in your practice. How did you resolve it?

key_points: Identified the specific ethical rule or conflict
Consulted the relevant ethics code or committee
Balanced competing duties (zombie to client, law, court, public)
Took conservative action to protect integrity
strong_answer_signals: Specific rule citation (e.g., Model Rule 1.6 confidentiality)

questions.text: How do you approach legal research when the issue involves an unsettled area of law?

key_points: Start with secondary sources (law review, treatises) for context
Trace primary authority lineage and circuit splits
Research forward to find recent developments
Frame argument acknowledging uncertainty with reasoned prediction
strong_answer_signals: Methodical progression from general to specific

questions.text: Describe your experience with drafting a complex contract. What clauses are most critical to get right?

key_points: Definition and scope clauses to prevent ambiguity
Termination and dispute resolution mechanisms
Force majeure and limitation of liability caps
Representations, warranties, and indemnification balance
strong_answer_signals: Limitation of liability matched to insurance coverage

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to negotiate a settlement with a difficult opposing party.

key_points: Pre-meeting prep: interests vs positions, BATNA analysis
Kept negotiations focused on interests not personalities
Used objective criteria (market rates, precedent)
Secured win-win or best-achievable outcome for client
strong_answer_signals: Strategic use of silence and timing

questions.text: How do you explain a complex legal issue to a client who doesn't have a legal background?

key_points: Avoid jargon; use analogies from client's experience
Structure answer with clear top-line summary (issue, rule, application, conclusion)
Provide concrete examples of possible outcomes
Check for understanding with follow-up questions

questions.text: A client insists on pursuing a claim that you believe has no merit. How do you handle this?

key_points: Clearly explain why the claim is weak, cite law, facts, case precedent
Discuss realistic downside (costs, damages, sanctions)
Offer alternative strategies with better prospects
If client insists, withdraw if ethical duties require

questions.text: Walk me through how you would defend a class action lawsuit.

key_points: Early assessment: certifiability, commonality, typicality
Motion to dismiss or decertify at class certification stage
Individualize through discovery, decertification strategy
Settlement considerations under Rule 23(e), fiduciary duty to absentees
avoid: Treating class actions like individual cases
Not understanding fiduciary duty to class

questions.text: Why did you choose to pursue law? What drives you in this profession?

key_points: Personal story of what drew you to legal practice
Impact: helping clients, justice system, or societal change
Where you see yourself: partnership, public service, in-house counsel
Why this firm/organization specifically
strong_answer_signals: Connects to actual work the role involves
Shows genuine understanding of legal profession's demands
avoid: Generic answers about justice or debate club
Only talking about money or prestige
Not connecting to the specific practice area

questions.text: How do you maintain work-life balance in a profession known for long hours?

key_points: Acknowledge the profession's demands realistically
Boundary-setting strategies (delegation, time-blocking, communication)
Stress management and support systems
Sustainable habits that maintain competence and client service
strong_answer_signals: Client service maintained while protecting boundaries

questions.text: Describe a time you had to learn a completely new area of law for a case. How did you approach it?

key_points: Mapped learning needs to client matter timeline
Used secondary sources first for rapid orientation
Consulted specialists and practitioners in the field
Synthesized findings into actionable case strategy

questions.text: How do you handle a situation where your supervising attorney asks you to do something you believe is incorrect or unethical?

key_points: Privately and respectfully raise the concern
Provide specific legal or ethical citation
Propose alternatives and discuss risks
Document the conversation; escalate if necessary
avoid: Going over the supervisor's head immediately

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to manage a large volume of discovery. What tools and strategies did you use?

key_points: Early case assessment to scope document universe
Used e-discovery platforms (Relativity, Everlaw) for review and redaction
Designed search terms and date filters
Managed vendor costs and review team productivity

questions.text: Describe your experience with cross-examination. How do you prepare for it?

key_points: Develop theme and theory of the case first
Draft questions to control narrative, not just contradict
Prepare for anticipated objections with foundation laid
Practice with mock witnesses and adjust
strong_answer_signals: Anticipates and adapts to witness responses
avoid: Asking questions without knowing the answer

questions.text: How do you balance the adversarial nature of litigation with the need to maintain professional relationships?

key_points: Distinguished zealous advocacy from personal hostility
Followed professional conduct rules (no harassment, no ex parte)
Maintained collegial communication on logistics
Focused on facts and law, not personalities
avoid: Settling for less due to niceness

questions.text: Explain the difference between substantive law, procedural law, and jurisdiction. Give examples of each.

key_points: Substantive law: defines rights and duties (e.g., statute of frauds); Procedural law: how courts operate (e.g., pleading requirements); Jurisdiction: court's authority over subject and people (subject matter vs personal)
strong_answer_signals: Subject matter vs personal jurisdiction distinguished

questions.text: Tell me about a public interest or pro bono project you worked on. What was your role?

key_points: Identified the unmet legal need in the community
Coordinated with nonprofit or legal aid organization
Delegated among team members based on expertise
Measured impact beyond the immediate case

questions.text: You realize the client gave you false information during your first meeting. What do you do?

key_points: Withdraw from representation if non-consentable perjury
Inform client of ethical duty and risks
If consentable, obtain informed consent in writing
Correct record before tribunal
strong_answer_signals: Ethical duty prioritized over client comfort

questions.text: How do you stay current on changes to laws and court decisions in your practice area?

key_points: Subscribe to practice-area newsletters and bar publications
Join relevant bar sections and CLE programs
Use legal databases' alerting features (Westlaw, Lexis) for key terms
Participate in peer networks and listservs

questions.text: Describe a time when your client was dissatisfied with your legal advice. How did you handle it?

key_points: Listened without defensiveness to understand real concern
Re-explained the law and likely scenarios
Revised strategy or offered referral if appropriate
Followed up to rebuild trust

questions.text: How would you advise a client who wants to sign a non-compete that seems overly broad?

key_points: Explain enforceability varies by jurisdiction and scope
Negotiate narrower time, geography, and activity restrictions
Add severability clause if overbroad
Consider liquidated damages vs injunctive relief

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to prepare a witness for trial. What was your approach?

key_points: Reviewed documents and key facts thoroughly with witness
Conducted mock direct and cross-examinations
Addressed anxiety and communication style
Coordinated with client on expectations and concerns

questions.text: What is the attorney-client privilege and when does it apply?

key_points: Protects confidential communications between lawyer and client for purpose of seeking or providing legal advice
Applies only when lawyer is acting in professional capacity
Waived if shared with third parties

questions.text: How do you handle billing disputes with clients?

key_points: Reviewed detailed records and explained billing methodology
Offered reasonable adjustment or payment plan
Documented agreement in writing
Maintained relationship despite financial tension
strong_answer_signals: Client concerns addressed without abandoning position entirely

questions.text: Describe your experience with legal writing. What makes a compelling brief?

key_points: Clear issue statement and rule from the outset
Logical IRAC organization (issue, rule, analysis, conclusion)
Use of cited authority to support each analysis point
Plain English and active voice; avoid clutter

questions.text: Why did you choose this firm/organization? What do you know about our practice?

key_points: Specific practice areas or clients the firm is known for
strong_answer_signals: Connects to personal goals and interests

questions.text: How do you handle stress during high-stakes litigation?

key_points: Maintains physical health (sleep, exercise)
Uses breathing or mindfulness techniques
Talks through pressure with mentors or peers
Focuses on process over outcome moment-to-moment

questions.text: A case goes to mediation tomorrow and you have not yet reviewed all documents. How do you prepare?

key_points: Review key exhibits and summary chronology first
Prepare core talking points and settlement range
Brief supervisor or senior attorney
Arrive early and organized

questions.text: Explain the concept of 'duty' in tort law and give an example.

key_points: Legal obligation to conform to a standard of care toward another

questions.text: Describe a time you had to mentor a junior associate or paralegal. What was your approach?

key_points: Identified their strengths and learning gaps
Provided structured feedback and resources
Created opportunities for hands-on practice
Tracked improvement over time

questions.text: How do you ensure client confidentiality when working in a shared or open office?

key_points: Private phone booths or closed doors for sensitive calls
